p: Implement `k_shortest_paths(n, edges, s, t, k)` returning up to k loopless (simple) paths from s to t in a directed graph with positive integer weights, as a list of (cost, [nodes...]) sorted by cost, then lexicographically by node list. edges = list of (u, v, w); parallel edges may exist (treat the cheapest as the only one). Use Yen's algorithm (Dijkstra for the spur paths with root-path nodes and deviated edges removed). Return fewer than k paths if fewer exist; return [] if t is unreachable. The test compares against exhaustive enumeration on random graphs of up to 9 nodes and checks a 200-node graph for k=10 within a few seconds.

Implement class `BloomFilter(m_bits, k_hashes)` with `add(item: bytes)`, `might_contain(item) -> bool`, `bit_positions(item) -> list[int]` and `count_set_bits()`. Hashing is fully specified so results are deterministic: h1 = SHA-256(item) as a big-endian integer, h2 = SHA-256(item + b'\x01') as a big-endian integer; position i (0-based, i < k) = (h1 + i*h2) mod m. Use the standard library hashlib for SHA-256. Also implement `union(other)` (same m and k required, else ValueError) and `estimated_count()` = -(m/k) * ln(1 - X/m) where X is the number of set bits, rounded to the nearest integer (0 when X == 0).
t:
import hashlib,math
b=BloomFilter(1000,3); h1=int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(b'cat').digest(),'big'); h2=int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(b'cat\x01').digest(),'big')
assert b.bit_positions(b'cat')==[(h1+i*h2)%1000 for i in range(3)]
assert not b.might_contain(b'cat'); b.add(b'cat'); assert b.might_contain(b'cat') and b.count_set_bits()<=3 and b.estimated_count()==1
b2=BloomFilter(1000,3); b2.add(b'dog'); u=b.union(b2); assert u.might_contain(b'cat') and u.might_contain(b'dog') and not b.might_contain(b'dog')
try: b.union(BloomFilter(999,3)); assert False
except ValueError: pass
big=BloomFilter(100000,7); items=[str(i).encode() for i in range(5000)]
for it in items: big.add(it)
assert all(big.might_contain(it) for it in items)
fp=sum(big.might_contain(str(i).encode()) for i in range(5000,15000))
assert fp<200, fp
X=big.count_set_bits(); assert big.estimated_count()==round(-(100000/7)*math.log(1-X/100000)) and 4700<big.estimated_count()<5300
assert BloomFilter(10,2).estimated_count()==0

p: Implement ISO 8601 week dates WITHOUT using datetime.isocalendar/fromisocalendar or strftime: `to_iso_week(y, m, d) -> (iso_year, iso_week, iso_weekday)` with weekday 1=Monday..7=Sunday, and `from_iso_week(iso_year, iso_week, iso_weekday) -> (y, m, d)`. You may use datetime.date arithmetic (toordinal/fromordinal/weekday) or do it from scratch. Also `weeks_in_year(iso_year)` returning 52 or 53. Handle years 1..9999 and raise ValueError for an invalid week or weekday. The test checks every day from 1900 to 2100 against the standard library.
t:
import datetime
assert to_iso_week(2026,1,1)==(2026,1,4) and to_iso_week(2027,1,1)==(2026,53,5) and to_iso_week(2024,12,30)==(2025,1,1)
assert from_iso_week(2026,53,5)==(2027,1,1) and from_iso_week(2025,1,1)==(2024,12,30)
assert weeks_in_year(2026)==53 and weeks_in_year(2025)==52 and weeks_in_year(2020)==53 and weeks_in_year(2021)==52
for bad in ((2025,53,1),(2026,54,1),(2026,1,8),(2026,0,1),(2026,1,0)):
    try: from_iso_week(*bad); assert False,bad
    except ValueError: pass
d=datetime.date(1900,1,1); end=datetime.date(2100,12,31)
while d<=end:
    y,w,wd=d.isocalendar(); r=to_iso_week(d.year,d.month,d.day); assert r==(y,w,wd),(d,r)
    assert from_iso_week(y,w,wd)==(d.year,d.month,d.day)
    d+=datetime.timedelta(days=1)
assert to_iso_week(1,1,1)==(1,1,1) and to_iso_week(9999,12,31)==(9999,52,5)

p:
Implement an RFC 4180 CSV reader and writer without the csv module: `parse_csv(text, delimiter=',') -> list[list[str]]` and `write_csv(rows, delimiter=',') -> str`. Fields may be quoted with double quotes; a quote inside a quoted field is escaped as two quotes; quoted fields may contain the delimiter and newlines (both 
 and 
); rows end with 
 or 
; an empty final line is not a row. Unquoted fields containing a quote character are a syntax error (ValueError), as is an unterminated quoted field. The writer must quote a field iff it contains the delimiter, a quote,  or 
, or leading/trailing spaces, and must terminate every row with 
. parse_csv(write_csv(rows)) must round-trip any rows of strings.
t:
import csv,io,random
assert parse_csv('a,b,c\n1,2,3\n')==[['a','b','c'],['1','2','3']]
assert parse_csv('a,"b,c",d\r\n')==[['a','b,c','d']]
assert parse_csv('"he said ' + '""hi""' + '",x')==[['he said "hi"','x']]
assert parse_csv('"multi\nline",1\n')==[['multi\nline','1']]
assert parse_csv('')==[] and parse_csv('\n')==[['']] and parse_csv('a,,\n')==[['a','','']]
assert parse_csv('a;b\n',delimiter=';')==[['a','b']]
for bad in ('a,b"c\n','"abc','"a"b,c\n'):
    try: parse_csv(bad); assert False,bad
    except ValueError: pass
assert write_csv([['a','b'],['1','2']])=='a,b\r\n1,2\r\n'
assert write_csv([['x,y','he said "hi"',' lead','trail ','plain']])=='"x,y","he said ""hi""' + '"," lead","trail ",plain\r\n'
random.seed(13); alphabet='ab,"\n\r ;x'
for _ in range(200):
    rows=[[''.join(random.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(random.randint(0,6))) for _ in range(random.randint(1,5))] for _ in range(random.randint(1,4))]
    rows=[[r[0] or 'q']+r[1:] for r in rows]   # the csv module reads a blank line as [] not [''], so keep first cells non-empty for the cross-check
    for delim in (',',';'):
        txt=write_csv(rows,delim); assert parse_csv(txt,delim)==rows,(rows,txt)
        assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(txt,newline=''),delimiter=delim))==rows

p: Implement `knapsack(items, capacity)` for the 0/1 knapsack problem where items is a list of (weight, value) with non-negative integer weights and POSITIVE integer values. Return (best_value, chosen) where chosen is a sorted list of item indices achieving best_value; among all optimal subsets return the one whose sorted index list is LEXICOGRAPHICALLY SMALLEST (so prefer including lower indices). Must be O(n*capacity) time using DP with reconstruction (the test uses 400 items and capacity 5,000). Zero-weight items with positive value must always be taken.
t:
import itertools,random
def _brute(items,cap):
    best=None
    for r in range(len(items)+1):
        for comb in itertools.combinations(range(len(items)),r):
            w=sum(items[i][0] for i in comb); v=sum(items[i][1] for i in comb)
            if w<=cap and (best is None or v>best[0] or (v==best[0] and list(comb)<best[1])): best=(v,list(comb))
    return best
assert knapsack([(1,1),(3,4),(4,5),(5,7)],7)==(9,[1,2])
assert knapsack([(2,3),(2,3),(2,3)],4)==(6,[0,1])
assert knapsack([(0,5),(10,1)],5)==(5,[0]) and knapsack([],10)==(0,[]) and knapsack([(5,1)],4)==(0,[])
random.seed(14)
for _ in range(60):
    n=random.randint(1,9); items=[(random.randint(0,7),random.randint(1,9)) for _ in range(n)]; cap=random.randint(0,15)
    assert knapsack(items,cap)==_brute(items,cap),(items,cap)
random.seed(15); items=[(random.randint(1,60),random.randint(1,100)) for _ in range(400)]
import time; t0=time.time(); v,ch=knapsack(items,5000); assert time.time()-t0<25
assert sum(items[i][0] for i in ch)<=5000 and sum(items[i][1] for i in ch)==v and ch==sorted(ch)

p: Implement a protobuf-style wire codec. `encode_varint(n)` / `decode_varint(buf, pos) -> (value, new_pos)` for unsigned 64-bit base-128 varints (little-endian groups of 7 bits, MSB continuation); `zigzag(n)` / `unzigzag(z)` for signed 64-bit values; and `encode_message(fields)` / `decode_message(buf)` where fields is a list of (field_number, wire_type, value): wire type 0 = varint (int, encoded as unsigned), 1 = fixed64 (int, little-endian 8 bytes), 2 = length-delimited (bytes), 5 = fixed32 (int, LE 4 bytes). The tag is encode_varint((field_number << 3) | wire_type). decode_message returns the list of (field_number, wire_type, value) in order and raises ValueError on truncation, an unknown wire type, or a varint longer than 10 bytes.
t:
assert encode_varint(0)==b'\x00' and encode_varint(1)==b'\x01' and encode_varint(300)==b'\xac\x02' and encode_varint(2**64-1)==b'\xff'*9+b'\x01'
assert decode_varint(b'\xac\x02\xff',0)==(300,2) and decode_varint(b'\x00\x01',1)==(1,2)
assert zigzag(0)==0 and zigzag(-1)==1 and zigzag(1)==2 and zigzag(-2)==3 and zigzag(2147483647)==4294967294 and zigzag(-2**63)==2**64-1
for v in (0,-1,1,-2,12345,-12345,2**63-1,-2**63): assert unzigzag(zigzag(v))==v
m=[(1,0,150),(2,2,b'testing'),(3,1,2**40),(4,5,7),(1,0,3)]
b=encode_message(m); assert b.startswith(b'\x08\x96\x01\x12\x07testing') and decode_message(b)==m
assert encode_message([])==b'' and decode_message(b'')==[]
for bad in (b'\x08', b'\x12\x05abc', b'\x0b\x00', b'\x08'+b'\xff'*11, b'\x19\x01\x02'):
    try: decode_message(bad); assert False,bad
    except ValueError: pass
import random; random.seed(16)
for _ in range(100):
    m=[]
    for _ in range(random.randint(0,6)):
        f=random.randint(1,2**29-1); wt=random.choice([0,1,2,5])
        v={0:random.randint(0,2**64-1),1:random.randint(0,2**64-1),2:bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(random.randint(0,20))),5:random.randint(0,2**32-1)}[wt]
        m.append((f,wt,v))
    assert decode_message(encode_message(m))==m

p: Implement class `Autocomplete` with `insert(word, weight)` (re-inserting a word REPLACES its weight), `delete(word)` (no-op if absent), and `top_k(prefix, k)` returning the k words starting with prefix ordered by weight descending, then word ascending. Use a trie; `top_k` must not scan the whole dictionary: the test inserts 200,000 words and then runs 20,000 queries with short prefixes on a large set and expects them to finish in a few seconds. Also `count(prefix)` returning how many stored words start with prefix, in O(len(prefix)) by maintaining subtree counts.

Implement `failure(s)` returning the KMP failure (prefix) function as a list where failure[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of s[:i+1] that is also a suffix; `find_all(pattern, text)` returning all (possibly overlapping) start indices using KMP in O(n+m); `period(s)` returning the smallest p such that s[i]==s[i+p] for all valid i (p may equal len(s)); and `is_rotation(a, b)`. The test uses a 2,000,000-character text and must finish in a few seconds, so naive search or Python's str.find is not acceptable for find_all (str.find would be fine for correctness but you must implement KMP).
t:
assert failure('abcabcd')==[0,0,0,1,2,3,0] and failure('aaaa')==[0,1,2,3] and failure('')==[]
assert find_all('aa','aaaa')==[0,1,2] and find_all('abc','xabcabc')==[1,4] and find_all('','abc')==[0,1,2,3] and find_all('x','')==[]
assert period('abcabcab')==3 and period('aaaa')==1 and period('abcd')==4 and period('')==0 and period('abab')==2
assert is_rotation('abcd','cdab') and not is_rotation('abcd','acbd') and is_rotation('','') and not is_rotation('a','ab')
import random; random.seed(19)
for _ in range(300):
    t=''.join(random.choice('ab') for _ in range(random.randint(0,30))); p=''.join(random.choice('ab') for _ in range(random.randint(1,4)))
    assert find_all(p,t)==[i for i in range(len(t)-len(p)+1) if t.startswith(p,i)],(p,t)
    per=next(q for q in range(1,len(t)+1) if all(t[i]==t[i+q] for i in range(len(t)-q))) if t else 0; assert period(t)==per,t
random.seed(20); T=''.join(random.choice('abc') for _ in range(2000000)); P='abcab'*3
import time; t0=time.time(); r=find_all(P,T); assert time.time()-t0<12
assert len(r)==T.count(P) or len(r)>=T.count(P)
